newsitem.title: USA: US Plains cattle market calm after busy week-trade.
newsitem.headline: US Plains cattle market calm after busy week-trade.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets were quiet following this week's active sales that sold out most showlists, feedlot sources said.
"We're done for the week, there won't be a market until the middle of next week," one Panhandle feedyard manager said.
Cattle owners were seen pricing cattle at $69.00 to $70.00 per cwt early next week, several sources said.

Sales this week were at $68.00, up $1.00 from last week's late activity but unchanged from most trades last week. Prices next week were expected to be underpinned by reduced cattle supplies and firm beef demand, sources said.
Showlists next week in the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area and Kansas were seen steady to smaller than this week, cattle feeders said.
Demand for cattle was so stong this week that some feedlots stayed extremely current by pulling cattle ahead from next week's lists, they said.
Firm beef demand was tied to retail buying for mid-month beef features and bookings for Memorial Day, May 26, holiday promotions, market sources said.
But support next week could be limited if beef demand slows, some sources said.
